stages.name: Seleucid crown
stages.desc: Held for a reigning Seleucid king

stages.name: Rival claimant
stages.desc: Held for a pretender or a rival king

stages.name: Ptolemaic
stages.desc: Garrisoned or ruled by the Ptolemies of Egypt

stages.name: Free city
stages.desc: Self-governing, dating its coins by its own era

states.name: Nabatieh
timeline: The hill country behind Tyre and Sidon, royal land and city territory
The hills stay royal land while Tyre goes free
The south is held for Antiochus IX Cyzicenus
Ituraean chiefs hold the hills toward Mount Hermon; Aristobulus I of Judaea wars on them

states.name: South
timeline: Tyre and Sidon, the great Phoenician ports, mint silver for Demetrius I
Tyre and Sidon now mint for King Alexander Balas
Ptolemy VI garrisons Tyre and Sidon on his march north
The garrisons are massacred; Tyre and Sidon mint for Demetrius II
Tyre and Sidon mint for Antiochus VII
Demetrius II returns to the throne
Tyre wins its freedom and begins a new era on its silver shekels (year 1 = 126/5 BC); Sidon still mints for the kings
Demetrius II, defeated and refused by his wife at Ptolemais, is killed at Tyre
Tyre stays free; Sidon mints silver for Antiochus IX (dated 113/2 BC)
Antiochus IX grants Sidon its freedom (111/0 BC): Tyre and Sidon are both free cities

states.name: Beqaa
timeline: The Beqaa valley (the Marsyas), royal land between Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon
Coele Syria is held for Antiochus IX Cyzicenus
The Ituraean princes of Chalcis rule the valley in all but name

states.name: North
timeline: Tripolis and Orthosia mint and pay taxes for King Demetrius I
Alexander Balas, victor over Demetrius I, is recognised as king
Ptolemy VI garrisons the coastal cities on his march to Antioch
After Ptolemy's death his garrisons are killed; the coast returns to Demetrius II
Antiochus VII Sidetes takes the throne and marries Cleopatra Thea
Demetrius II, freed by the Parthians, reigns again
The coast south of Antioch falls to Antiochus IX Cyzicenus, rival of his half-brother
Tripolis mints silver for Antiochus IX (coins dated 105/4 BC)

states.name: Mount Lebanon
timeline: Byblos and the mountain villages under the Seleucid kings
Ptolemy VI's army marches up the coast through Byblos
Byblos returns to Demetrius II
Antiochus VII restores royal control of the coast
Byblos and its coast are held for Antiochus IX Cyzicenus
Ituraean chiefs dominate the mountain and raid Byblos; a local tyrant rises in the city

states.name: Beirut
timeline: Berytus, renamed Laodicea in Phoenicia, mints royal bronze
Ptolemy VI's garrison holds the city
Back under Demetrius II
The usurper Diodotus Tryphon, who has just killed the boy-king Antiochus VI, holds the coast
Tryphon sacks Berytus for siding with Demetrius II
Antiochus VII hunts Tryphon down; the coast returns to the crown
Held for Antiochus IX Cyzicenus

events.title: Balas at Ptolemais
events.text: Alexander Balas, who claims to be a son of Antiochus IV, seizes Ptolemais with Ptolemaic and Roman blessing.

events.title: Jonathan won over
events.text: Balas makes Jonathan Maccabaeus high priest, buying Judaean support against Demetrius I.

events.title: Demetrius I falls
events.text: King Demetrius I is killed in battle against Balas near Antioch.

events.title: Wedding at Ptolemais
events.text: Ptolemy VI gives his daughter Cleopatra Thea, about fourteen, to Balas in a royal wedding at Ptolemais.

events.title: Demetrius II lands
events.text: Demetrius I's teenage son lands with Cretan mercenaries to win back his father's throne.

events.title: Ptolemy marches north
events.text: Ptolemy VI leads his army up the Phoenician coast, leaving garrisons in every city.

events.title: A daughter remarried
events.text: Ptolemy takes Cleopatra Thea from Balas and gives her to Demetrius II.

events.title: Crown of Asia refused
events.text: Antioch offers Ptolemy VI the Seleucid crown; he declines it in favour of Demetrius II.

events.title: Battle of the Oenoparas
events.text: Balas is defeated near Antioch and killed while fleeing; Ptolemy VI dies of his wounds days later.

events.title: Antiochus VI proclaimed
events.text: The general Diodotus Tryphon crowns Balas's small son by Cleopatra Thea and takes Antioch.

events.title: Ladder of Tyre
events.text: Jonathan's brother Simon is made governor from the Ladder of Tyre to the borders of Egypt.

events.title: Tryphon crowns himself
events.text: Tryphon has the boy-king Antiochus VI killed and rules as king in his own name.

events.title: Berytus sacked
events.text: Tryphon destroys Berytus, which had sided with Demetrius II.

events.title: A king captured
events.text: Demetrius II marches east against Parthia and is taken prisoner.

events.title: Third husband
events.text: Cleopatra Thea, holding Seleucia, calls in Demetrius's brother Antiochus VII and marries him.

events.title: Siege of Dor
events.text: Antiochus VII besieges Tryphon in the coastal fortress of Dor; Tryphon escapes by sea.

events.title: Tryphon's end
events.text: Cornered at Apamea, Tryphon takes his own life.

events.title: March on Parthia
events.text: Antiochus VII leads a great army east to free Mesopotamia and his brother.

events.title: Demetrius returns
events.text: Antiochus VII is killed in Media; the Parthians release Demetrius II, who reclaims Antioch and his wife.

events.title: Zabinas proclaimed
events.text: While Demetrius meddles in Egypt, Antioch revolts and Ptolemy VIII backs a new pretender, Alexander Zabinas.

events.title: Tyre goes free
events.text: Tyre breaks with the kings and begins dating its silver shekels from its own year one.

events.title: Defeat at Damascus
events.text: Zabinas defeats Demetrius II near Damascus.

events.title: Gates shut
events.text: Demetrius flees to Ptolemais, but Cleopatra Thea has the gates closed against her husband.

events.title: Death at Tyre
events.text: Demetrius II takes ship for Tyre and is killed there on the orders of its governor.

events.title: Seleucus V killed
events.text: Thea has her eldest son Seleucus V killed after he takes the crown without her.

events.title: The queen alone
events.text: Cleopatra Thea issues silver in her own name and portrait, as sole ruler of the kingdom.

events.title: Zabinas executed
events.text: Antiochus VIII Grypus, Thea's second son and co-ruler, defeats and executes Zabinas.

events.title: The poisoned cup
events.text: Grypus, suspecting his mother, forces her to drink the poisoned wine she offered him.

events.title: Cyzicenus returns
events.text: Antiochus IX, Thea's son by Antiochus VII, returns from Cyzicus to claim the throne.

events.title: Antioch taken
events.text: Cyzicenus seizes Antioch; Sidon mints his silver.

events.title: Cleopatra IV killed
events.text: Grypus retakes Antioch; his queen Tryphaena has her own sister, Cyzicenus's wife, killed in a sanctuary.

events.title: Sidon goes free
events.text: Antiochus IX grants Sidon its freedom; it becomes a sacred, inviolable and autonomous city.

events.title: Seleucia free
events.text: Seleucia in Pieria, the port of Antioch, wins its freedom and a new era.

events.title: Lathyros in Cyprus
events.text: Ptolemy IX, driven from Egypt by his mother Cleopatra III, rules from Cyprus.

events.title: Tripolis mints
events.text: Tripolis strikes silver for Antiochus IX; within a few years it too gains autonomy.

events.title: Ituraeans attacked
events.text: Aristobulus I of Judaea annexes part of the Ituraean hill country.

events.title: Ptolemais besieged
events.text: Alexander Jannaeus besieges Ptolemais; Ptolemy IX lands from Cyprus to relieve it.

events.title: Cleopatra III's army
events.text: Cleopatra III marches up the coast and takes Ptolemais from her son.

events.title: Grypus murdered
events.text: Antiochus VIII is murdered by his minister Heracleon; the civil wars go on.

chartNote: Share of the area of present-day Lebanon by who held it each year. The regions are today's governorates, not the ancient cities' territories: the South stands for Tyre and Sidon, coloured free from Tyre's era of 126/5 BC (Sidon followed in 111/0 BC). Control often changed within a year and the sources are thin; this is a simplification.
